clue.text: Solitary. Scotsman -with wine around

parts.note: mon is the Scots dialect form of man
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine
C stands for circa, Latin for around

explanation.surface: A lone Scot sits with a glass of wine about him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mon' is how a Scotsman says 'man'; C (circa) is the standard abbreviation for 'around' in dates.
explanation.definitionFit: A monk's way of life is one of seclusion, so the adjective describes a solitary existence.

clue.text: People bathe in the hills

parts.note: men means people
a dip is a quick bathe

explanation.surface: Folk take a swim up in the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mendips are a range of hills in Somerset, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mendip Hills are a limestone range in Somerset in England.

clue.text: Officer with a public following

parts.note: an official whose title is always followed by the word public

explanation.surface: A popular official with many fans.
explanation.walkthrough: The full title is 'notary public', so the word 'public' follows him.
explanation.definitionFit: A notary public is an officer who certifies legal documents.

clue.text: Parasite thrown up in defeat

definitions.meaning: a boxer's second throws in this to concede

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a freeloader and also the item a boxer's corner throws up to concede a fight.

clue.text: Later Miami could be unimportant

indicators.note: the letters of the two words could be rearranged into something else

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trip to Miami later on might not matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something immaterial is irrelevant and of no consequence.

clue.text: Modern humour meets with success

parts.note: wit is clever humour
a hit is a success, as in a hit record

explanation.surface: A comedian's up-to-date jokes go down well.
explanation.definitionFit: Being 'with it' is an informal idiom for being fashionable and up to date.

clue.text: tis mad — - to make the service greater than the god" (T, and C)

definitions.text: tis mad — - to make the service greater than the god" (T, and C)

parts.words: tis mad — - to make the service greater than the god" (T, and C)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Troilus and Cressida about valuing worship over what is worshipped

explanation.surface: Hector's line from Troilus and Cressida with one word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Hector says ''Tis mad idolatry To make the service greater than the god' in Troilus and Cressida (T and C), Act 2.
explanation.definitionFit: Worship of images over the real deity, which is what the line accuses.

clue.text: Surprise prohibition on time for West Indian dance

parts.note: ha is an exclamation of surprise
a ban is a prohibition
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A shock ban on the hour for a Caribbean dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The habanera comes from Havana in Cuba, a West Indian island.
explanation.definitionFit: The habanera is a slow Cuban dance named after Havana.

clue.text: True, Roly' can upset the present government

indicators.note: upset means the letters are knocked over into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man called Roly could topple the current administration.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle dates from a time of Conservative (Tory) government in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: When this was set Britain was governed by the Conservatives, whose nickname is Tories.

clue.text: Memo about protocol — hardly my cup of tea

indicators.note: the word for the memo goes round the outside of the other piece, as about means surrounding

parts.note: a note is a short memo
form is correct procedure or etiquette, as in good form

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses an office memo about procedure as dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms of polite refusal, saying something does not suit one's taste.

clue.text: Terrorist — one from South Africa surrounds the doctor

indicators.note: the South African word is placed around the outside of the doctor's letters

parts.note: a Boer is a South African of Dutch descent
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A South African extremist holds a physician hostage.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who plants or drops bombs causes terror, so a bomber can be a terrorist.

clue.text: Wet, and angry about the trick

indicators.note: the word for angry wraps around the trick, as about means encircling here

parts.note: irate means angry
a rig is a swindle or trick, as in rigging a vote

explanation.surface: Someone soaked and furious complains about a prank.
explanation.definitionFit: To water land or flush a wound is to make it wet, a verb sense.

clue.text: "The royal — , and all quality" (Othello)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: Othello's farewell speech lists the royal flag carried in war

explanation.surface: A line from Othello's farewell to the pomp of war, with one word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The full line is 'The royal banner, and all quality, Pride, pomp, and circumstance of glorious war!' from Othello Act 3.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word is the royal flag carried before an army.

clue.text: A cab after dark for an absconder

parts.note: a fly was a light horse-drawn cab for hire
by night means after dark

explanation.surface: Someone flees by taxi under cover of night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' is an old word for a hired horse-drawn carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A fly-by-night is someone who slips away to avoid debts or duties.

clue.text: The test for one who drinks and drives is really in the country

definitions.text: The test for one who drinks and drives
definitions.meaning: a tongue-twister once used by police to test whether a driver's speech was slurred
truly means really and rural means of the countryside

explanation.walkthrough: Before breath tests, a suspected drunk driver might be asked to say this hard phrase clearly.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a famous speech test for drunkenness and a plain description of being genuinely rustic.

clue.text: In which God was our help

definitions.text: In which God was our help

parts.words: In which God was our help
parts.note: points to the opening line of Isaac Watts's hymn about God's help in former times

explanation.surface: A line of thanks for divine help in times gone by.
explanation.walkthrough: The hymn 'O God, our help in ages past' by Isaac Watts is sung at British remembrance services.
explanation.definitionFit: The hymn names former times as the era when God helped us.

clue.text: A word of command suggests a change from 8

definitions.text: A word of command suggests a change from 8

parts.words: A word of command suggests a change from 8
parts.note: a drill order that also hints at a political swing away from a Conservative government

explanation.surface: A drill sergeant's order hints at a change of government.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is TORY RULE; a swing to the political left would replace it, and the phrase is also a marching order.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a drill command and also a swing to the political left away from Conservative rule.

clue.text: In France Tuesday includes a hail of copper coin

indicators.note: the French word for Tuesday holds the greeting inside it

parts.note: mardi is French for Tuesday
ave is the Latin greeting, hail

explanation.surface: A French Tuesday event features a greeting for an old coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The maravedi was an old Spanish coin, later struck in copper.

clue.text: Iff A solitary star -could make Bogart rage

indicators.note: the letters of the two words could be rearranged to make something else

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A reclusive film star's antics might enrage Humphrey Bogart.
explanation.walkthrough: The Swedish actress is famous for the line 'I want to be alone', hence 'solitary star'; 'Iff' at the start is stray print.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hollywood actress was famed for her reclusiveness and her line about wanting to be alone.

clue.text: Colour sounds like a town in Oxfordshire

indicators.note: sounds like says the colour is said the same as the town

parts.note: Bicester is a market town in Oxfordshire, pronounced as two syllables

explanation.surface: A paint shade named after an English market town.
explanation.walkthrough: Bicester, a town north of Oxford, is pronounced 'Bister'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bistre is a brown pigment made from soot.

clue.text: People with a stomach — take it on the chin

parts.note: men means people
tum is a child's word for stomach

explanation.surface: Folk with guts take a punch on the chin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take it on the chin' sounds like the idiom for bearing a blow, but only 'chin' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Mentum is the anatomical Latin term for the chin.

clue.text: A strange resort for one who hoards.

indicators.note: strange means the letters of resort are put into an odd new order

explanation.surface: An odd holiday spot for a miser.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoarder stockpiles supplies, keeping them in reserve.

clue.text: Ruler receives a blow after a day

indicators.note: the blow comes after the day, so it is placed second

parts.note: Sat is the abbreviation for Saturday
a rap is a sharp knock or blow

explanation.surface: A monarch is struck one day.
explanation.definitionFit: A satrap was a provincial governor in ancient Persia, a kind of ruler.

clue.text: A happening in the Yard upsetting ten

parts.note: taken as written
the CID, Criminal Investigation Department, is based at Scotland Yard, London's police headquarters

indicators.note: upsetting means the letters of ten are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Something happens at Scotland Yard that upsets ten people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upsetting' turns TEN into ENT. Scotland Yard is the London police headquarters, home of the CID detectives.
explanation.definitionFit: An incident is an event or occurrence.

clue.text: Perception — that's the last word to use about the copper

indicators.note: the last word goes around the copper, as about means surrounding

parts.note: amen is said at the end of a prayer, the final word
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Insight is the final word to use about a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but gives the chemical symbol CU.
explanation.definitionFit: Acumen is sharp discernment or insight.

clue.text: A good mixer, but a trouble maker

definitions.meaning: a stirring device that shakes things up
a political stirrer who rouses others to protest

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a machine that stirs or shakes and a person who stirs up unrest.

clue.text: Not the type of bowling that wins Test matches

definitions.text: Not the type of bowling that wins Test matches

parts.words: Not the type of bowling that wins Test matches
parts.note: a contrast between the bowling done in cricket Test matches and the game of knocking down skittles in an alley

explanation.surface: A remark that one style of bowling is useless to a cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, Test matches are won by bowlers; this is the alley game with skittles, a different 'bowling'.
explanation.definitionFit: The game with ten skittles is called bowling but has nothing to do with cricket.

clue.text: A bad cold makes you flag

definitions.meaning: with a heavy cold your nose and eyes run, so you become one who streams
a long narrow pennant or ribbon

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both someone whose nose runs and a long narrow banner or pennant.
